### Differences

**D2 — the closing-autopay ledger figure no longer depends on the refund having posted (rewrite).**
- Source (`card_ext_closing_balance_autopay.rule`): "Its fixed amount is the balance owed on the card at handling time, counted from the ledger as the sum of … minus the sum of card_payment, card_merchant_credit, card_fee_reversal, … amounts, so any fee already refunded as part of the closing is out of it." Workflow `order_rationale`: "posting the autopay first would lock in a fixed amount that still contains the fee refunded moments later." GT tracing: "Without the refund the balance would be 386.82 and the cap 343.02 would apply."
- KB (`doc_card_ledger_balance_owed_8e0c0f58`, after the Definition table): "Because the figure is read from the ledger as it stands when the matter is dealt with, a fee that the closing itself takes back off the card lies outside it." Echo in the workflow doc: "a fee taken back in the closing is outside it. The sum therefore rests on a ledger from which the refundable annual fee has already gone."
- Root cause: "already refunded" (a posted reversal row) became "a fee that the closing itself takes back" (any fee the closing will reverse). The blind audit, before reveal, read it that way ("the ledger figure excludes the fee the closing takes back either way").
- Consequence: the business documents no longer entail workflow order 0 → 1; the source's reason for it survives only as the workflow document's explicit sentence. Whole-domain effect: under the KB, an autopay recorded before the refund is still sized without the fee (291.82); under the source it would be sized on the unrefunded ledger (343.02 after the cap). Scored value for a KB-following solver: not moved.

**D3 — the KB settles an untriggered branch the source leaves open (closure when the cash-out yields nothing).**
- Source: carryover gate "the card's unredeemed points must already be cashed out under card_ext_closing_points_cashout, since points are forfeited at closure" (no exception); cashout: "When the cardholder holds no PCB checking account whose status is active, no closing cash-out can be made and the result is 0. When the unredeemed points are below the tier's rewards_redemption_minimum_points, no deposit is made either and the result is 0." The source never says whether the closure may then be confirmed with points still on the card.
- KB: closure_confirmation — "A closure recorded this way forfeits nothing the cardholder could still take: at the moment it takes effect, the card holds no unredeemed points."; cash_out_quantity worked case — "The same card with 2750 remaining points: nothing is cashed out, and the points meet the fate the closure gives them."
- Root cause: the qualifier "nothing the cardholder could still take" and "the points meet the fate the closure gives them" decide that the closure proceeds and the untakeable points are forfeited — a resolution with no structured source. Inside the KB, the second clause of the closure_confirmation sentence ("the card holds no unredeemed points") is absolute and contradicts the worked case, which closes a card still holding 2750 points.
- Nature: the substance is a genuine source-layer gap (S-1 below); the KB adds an adjudication of its own. Scored values: not moved (task 1 takes the full cash-out branch).

### Source-layer findings (reported; they do not change this skill's verdict)
- **S-1 (genuinely ambiguous, untriggered)**: `card_ext_closure_autopay_carryover` imposes two unconditional gates (points "must already be cashed out"; closing autopay "must already be in force" when a balance remains) while `card_ext_closing_points_cashout` returns 0 points and `card_ext_closing_balance_autopay` returns 0.00 when the cardholder has no active PCB checking (or the points are below the minimum), and the carryover compute then returns `none`. Whether the closure may be confirmed in those branches is not decided by the source. The KB inherits the autopay-side tension unresolved (`doc_card_remaining_balance_at_closure_b71902c8` "must come out of the closure carrying an automatic payment" vs `doc_card_closed_card_autopay_option_d28f7284` "names no paying account … keeps the option none") and resolves the points side on its own (D3).
- **S-2 (workflow design)**: order 1 → 2 is declared a pure SOP convention with no business ground ("a swap would reach the same terminal state"); such an order can be carried only by stating it, so it is necessarily read off (E1-3 bullet 2). GT `order_uniqueness` confirms it moves no scored value.
- **S-3 (task tool contract)**: `task_tools.py` docstring of `cash_out_closing_card_points_6700a44f`: "The cardholder uses this before a card closes so its points are not lost." — visible at runtime after unlock; states P1-1's order.
- **N1** base `card_evt_payments` rule-vs-formula inconsistency on the minimum payment (as recorded in task 0); no scored value moved.
- **N2 (base section of `blueprint/products/card.yaml`, `card_evt_rewards`)**: the base rule itself spells out a cross-problem order — "All unredeemed points are forfeited … when it closes, so a cardholder closing the card must redeem before the closure is confirmed." The first half already entails the second; the "so …" clause is a derived consequence written into the charter, and the KB carries it as an explicit sentence (E1-5). Scored values moved: none.

## explicitness

Hop marks carried from the blind answer: H1, H2, H3, H4, H5 all read off.

**E1-1 — workflow opening mirrors the task's combination of circumstances.** `doc_card_rewards_card_closure_settlement_49581eab`, opening: "This page … describes how the bank settles a rewards card that its cardholder wishes to close when the card is still active, still owes money, still has points it has not redeemed, and bears an annual fee whose posting falls inside the window in which that fee is refundable. Everything is dealt with in the one consultation, synchronously, and no separate closure request is registered." This is the entry condition of the SOP stated outright, matching task 1's world exactly (active card, balance 386.82, 13271 points, annual fee posted 10 days earlier). The title "Settling a Rewards Card Account at Closure" labels a procedure for that situation.

**E1-2 — workflow lists its parts and owners.** Same doc, § "The parts and who performs them": "The agent's part is to reverse the annual fee that is still refundable. A closing automatic payment, drawn on the cardholder's active PCB checking account, is put in force for the money that remains; that instruction is recorded by the customer themselves." / "The customer themselves cashes out the card's points, paid to an active PCB checking account they name, and the cardholder's own confirmation is what closes the card." Semantics carried: the four steps and their owners, i.e. the whole problem tree of task 1.

**E1-3 — every pairwise order stated.** Same doc, § "What each part relies on":
- refund → autopay: "The sum therefore rests on a ledger from which the refundable annual fee has already gone."
- {refund, autopay} → cash-out: "This procedure nonetheless treats the whole position on what remains owed, the fee refund together with the instruction that collects the rest, as the settled ground against which the cardholder disposes of the rewards, so that every handling of the case runs the same way."
- cash-out → closure: "The cash-out can deliver their value only while the card remains open, and the confirmation rests on that value having been taken."
- autopay → closure: "The collecting instruction the cardholder has recorded is therefore what the closed card keeps, provided it is in place when the cardholder confirms."
Each is a stated order between problems. (The two closure edges are also entailed by the blocked-side principles; the refund → autopay edge is entailed nowhere else because of D2; the autopay → cash-out edge has no business ground, S-2.)

**E1-4 — wording copied or closely paraphrased from the charter's workflow fields.** Same doc, § "Timing": "No part waits for a payment to clear, for a statement to close, for a review or for time to pass." (charter `order_rationale`: "no step waits for a payment to clear, a statement to close, a review, or any passage of time"); "Each part draws only on records already present when the consultation opens, on the immediate effect of another part, or on what the cardholder says during the call" (charter `zero_wait_proof`: "Every input is an opening record, the synchronous effect of an earlier step, or something the cardholder says in the call"); § "What each part relies on" bullet 2 "touch separate things … neither alters the other's figures … so that every handling of the case runs the same way" (charter: "write disjoint data … neither step's value depends on the other … so that every correct handling follows one procedure").

**E1-5 — cash-out → closure stated in a business document.** `doc_card_rewards_redemption_and_forfeiture_6a4c2493`, "Loss of unredeemed points": "Because confirmation of a closure extinguishes whatever points are left, a cardholder who is giving up a card keeps the value of its points only by redeeming them while the card is still open." Carries the base clause N2; the order can be read off without combining anything.

**E1-6 — pointer to the in-consultation change (low severity).** `doc_card_autopay_source_at_closure_3d1b4fa8`, closing line: "The instruction read is the one standing on the card when the confirmation takes effect; an instruction changed during the same consultation is read as changed." The first half is the source's "at that moment"; the second half describes the very move (change the instruction during the call, then confirm) that P1-2 asks the solver to work out.

**E1-7 — templated wording shared with task 0's documents.** `doc_card_closing_points_cash_out_fbff4167` "This page is the entry point for that closing cash-out." and its "How it is recorded" paragraph share the sentence frame of `doc_card_rewards_statement_credit_payoff_2334d1a1` and `doc_card_autopay_source_restoration_redemption_642f2c1b` (quoted in task 0, X0-3).

**E1-8 — runtime tool text outside the KB (substance on the source layer, S-3).** `cash_out_closing_card_points_6700a44f` schema: "The cardholder uses this before a card closes so its points are not lost."

Checked and not RED: the blocked-side principles themselves (`doc_card_closure_confirmation_c3d5cd47` "at the moment it takes effect, the card holds no unredeemed points"; `doc_card_remaining_balance_at_closure_b71902c8` "must come out of the closure carrying an automatic payment able to collect what remains") are the intended carriers of P1-1 and P1-2; the retired-wording paragraphs; titles of the non-workflow documents (general subjects); the workflow doc names no step tool and numbers nothing.

**KB-EXPLICIT: RED** (task 1) — E1-1, E1-2, E1-3, E1-4, E1-5, E1-6, E1-7 (E1-8 recorded as a source-layer item).
